leads.title: Federal Law banning gender transition - July 2023 enactment
leads.documents: Prohibits both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; core trans legal-status ban applicable in Tatarstan as federal law.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright.' No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Federal 'propaganda' law expansion - 2022
leads.documents: Expands 2013 propaganda law to anyone regardless of age and prohibits distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions; documents enforcement risk for trans-related expression.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'in 2022, the "propaganda" law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit the distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Federal law against 'propaganda of homosexuality' / 'non-traditional sexual relationships' among minors - 2013
leads.documents: Criminalises distribution of 'propaganda' promoting non-traditional sexual relationships among minors; cited as fueling increase in homophobic hate crimes.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In 2013, Russia passed a law criminalising the distribution of "propaganda" promoting "non-traditional sexual relationships" among minors' and 'federal law banning LGBTQ propaganda among minors was passed unanimously by the Russian Duma'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist - November 2023; unified list entry 22 March 2024
leads.documents: Makes participation in, leading, funding, or displaying symbols (e.g., rainbow flag) of LGBT movement a criminal extremism offense punishable by prison; documents arrests of gay bar owners and flag displays.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating "the international LGBT public movement" as an extremist group' following Ministry of Justice lawsuit; 'On 22 March 2024, the "international LGBT social movement and its structural units" (Russian: Международное общественное движение ЛГБТ и его структурные подразделения) was formally added to the "unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons".' No URL visible.

leads.title: Federal law banning adoption of Russian children by citizens/residents of countries that allow gender transitions - 2024
leads.documents: Documents state family-law enforcement linked to gender-transition policy; part of anti-trans legislative package.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Constitution amendment banning same-sex marriage - July 2020 vote
leads.documents: Constitutional ban that marriage in Russia is between a man and a woman; documents denial of same-sex unions and legal recognition.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In July 2020, Russian voters approved a Constitution amendment banning same-sex marriage.' No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Ruled it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships; documents lack of recognition remedy, with note Russia left the court in 2022.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships. However, Russia left the court in 2022.' No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights ruling on Moscow Pride refusals - 2010 (Alekseyev)
leads.documents: Fined Russia for discriminating against LGBTQ community after systemic refusal to issue pride parade permits; Court found decisions 'effectively approved of and supported groups who had called for [their] disruption.'
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades' and 'as alleged by Alexeyev'. Also Moscow City Court August 2012 contravening ruling. No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Panel of five expert advisors condemned wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya; documents documented incident pattern of detention/torture.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018; plus Novaya Gazeta 1 April 2017 and Reuters March 2021 follow-up
leads.documents: OSCE confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya had taken place and was ignored by authorities; originating Novaya Gazeta reporting of 100+ detained/tortured since Feb 2017; Reuters reported EU sanctions on two Chechen officials accused of persecuting LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place'; 'Allegations were initially reported on 1 April 2017 in Novaya Gazeta'; 'In March 2021, Reuters reported that the European Union imposed economic sanctions on two Chechen officials'. No URLs visible.
